summary: In 2008 Chinese dairy giant Sanlu and dozens of rivals sold infant formula laced with melamine to fake protein tests, then hid it through the Beijing Olympics, sickening some 300,000 babies.

evidence.note: Sanlu (Three Deer) founded as a state dairy in 1956; its Mao-era history opens the story
1986 shift to loaning cows to indebted smallholders, framed as early gig work
2005 partnership with New Zealand's Fonterra, which takes a large stake
2004 fake formula scandal in which infants starved, and the crackdown that followed
price controls push middlemen to add melamine to pass nitrogen-based protein tests
first documented poisoning case, a father who bought formula in November 2007
Sanlu with party backing blocks a full recall, plants stories and buys search results
Fonterra tells NZ consulate; PM Helen Clark raises it with Beijing in September 2008
22 other firms implicated; executions, prison terms and compensation follow
lasting distrust of Chinese dairy, a later fake milk case, and food insecurity of the poor today

notes: Reverse episode researched and told by Mia Wong. Transcript places Sanlu in the province containing Wuhan (Hubei); Sanlu was actually based in Shijiazhuang, Hebei, so no subdivision is given. Covered span starts at Sanlu's 1956 founding since its state-era history gets real airtime; the 2009 executions close it. Beijing Olympics cover-up kept as a keyword rather than the sports theme. US comparisons (Nike, Nestle, contract growers) left out of setting.
